thesisQuality.note: Strong current demand/capacity evidence and domestic expansion support a durable problem, but commodity economics constrain value-capture durability.

financialOperatingMomentum.note: Q2 sales, shipments, adjusted EBITDA, liquidity and Q3 guidance are strong, tempered by equipment-failure and commodity-cycle sensitivity.

marketValuationOpportunity.note: September 2026 market capitalization near $3.86B follows major appreciation while earnings remain commodity-sensitive; headroom is not clearly compelling on available evidence.

catalystScore.note: Mt. Holly expansion is operating and Oklahoma engineering/JV/power milestones provide material identifiable catalysts, though definitive agreements remain pending.

governancePower.note: Independent chairman, independent audit committee and formal risk oversight support adequate-to-strong governance; insider ownership is modest and evidence does not justify an exceptional band.

alignment2036.note: Primary aluminum is a foundational industrial input and planned domestic capacity directly addresses infrastructure and supply-chain resilience across multiple long-duration demand themes.

crossDivisionLeverage.note: U.S./Iceland smelting plus 55% bauxite/alumina JV participation provides several operating exposures, but economics remain substantially linked to one commodity complex.

bottleneckControl.note: Century controls scarce operating U.S. primary-aluminum capacity and participates in a potentially system-material expansion, but power and commodity inputs remain external constraints.

scenarioRobustness.note: Geographic and upstream integration improve resilience, but earnings remain exposed to aluminum premiums, power cost and smelter reliability.

substitutionResilience.note: Primary aluminum has broad industrial uses and domestic capacity has strategic relevance, but Century sells a globally traded commodity with alternative producers and materials.

supplyChainResilience.note: Jamalco upstream participation and U.S./European production add resilience, while power, alumina and operational reliability remain material dependencies.

pricingPower.note: Current margins benefit from constrained supply and favorable aluminum economics, but global commodity pricing limits durable company-specific price control.

risk.note: Material commodity, power, equipment reliability and large-project financing/execution exposures offset strong current liquidity and operating results.

confidence.note: Recent issuer results are corroborated by SEC filings/proxy and independent current market data; final Oklahoma financing/power economics and normalized-cycle profitability remain unknown.

thesis: Century combines scarce existing U.S. primary-aluminum capacity, upstream integration and credible domestic expansion optionality with strong current operating momentum, but value remains constrained by commodity/power cyclicality and unresolved project economics.
keyRisk: Normalized aluminum/power economics or Oklahoma financing and power terms may fail to support the current earnings/expansion case.
nextCatalyst: Definitive Oklahoma JV/power agreements and construction-start evidence, alongside Q3 2026 operating results.

scoreBreakdown.formula: weighted components - (risk*0.16), then multiplied by max(0.8,dataConfidence/100)
